transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m kind of embarrassed to say it, but I’m here because I’ve been having a really hard time with rats. Even just the thought that I might see one, like in an old building or a trash room at work, has gotten so bad that I’m avoiding parts of my cleaning job. I know it’s probably not actually dangerous, but I just… I can’t seem to make myself do it sometimes.
Is your fear mainly just about rats?

Yes… mostly rats. I mean, that’s the thing that really gets to me. Even thinking I might see one in an old building or the trash room at work, I kind of freeze up, and lately it’s been bad enough that I can’t do some parts of my cleaning job. I know that probably sounds silly, because it’s not like it’s always actually dangerous, but… it’s rats, mainly.
When you see a rat, or think you might see one, do you feel a sudden rush of intense fear or panic?

Yes… I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, but it does hit me really fast. If I hear scratching near a wall or see something move by a pipe, my whole body just reacts before I can think. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I have to get out of there right away. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel that your fear of rats is stronger than the actual danger they usually pose?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I know rats aren’t usually going to, you know, attack me or anything, and it’s probably just because I’m in old buildings or trash rooms for work. But the fear feels way bigger than that. It’s gotten to where just thinking I might see one can make me avoid parts of my job, which… I know isn’t really reasonable. Is that what you mean?
